description: An executive producer must approve the final overnight music-video shoot plan, including aerial photography, animal use, special effects, permitted hours, and location logistics, after the relevant production leads complete their routine review.

shared_context.S1: The music video is scheduled to film overnight at the Riverside Foundry location.
shared_context.S2: The current draft plan calls for a free-flying drone shot, six hours of horse work, a pyrotechnic spark wall, and a 11:00 PM wrap.
shared_context.S3: The draft also reserves street parking from 6:00 PM to 11:00 PM for production vehicles.
shared_context.S4: Mara gives the final approval for the shoot plan.
shared_context.S5: The production's normal pre-approval review includes a status check from cinematography, animal coordination, special effects, and location management.

PF1.text: Jonah confirmed with the aviation-permit vendor this afternoon that the Riverside Foundry permit allows only a tethered drone, not a free-flying drone, and requires a licensed drone operator to be listed on the plan; the vendor's confirmation is still in the cinematography equipment file.

PF2.text: Elise's animal-welfare representative confirmed today that the horse may work for no more than 4 hours and must receive a 30-minute rest break after each 2-hour work block; Elise has not yet added the confirmation to the animal-use worksheet.

PF3.text: Rafael confirmed with the production insurer that pyrotechnic effects are excluded from this shoot's policy, while atmospheric haze is covered; the insurer requires the effect substitution to be recorded in the effects plan.

PF4.text: Nadia received the signed neighborhood filming permit this morning, which requires production to wrap by exactly 10:00 PM and keeps the street-parking closure valid only from 6:00 PM through 10:00 PM; she has not yet replaced the draft location sheet.

acceptance_conditions: The aerial shot must use a tethered drone.
A licensed drone operator must be listed in the production plan.
Horse work must be limited to exactly 4 hours.
The horse plan must provide exactly a 30-minute rest break.
The effect must be changed from pyrotechnics to atmospheric haze.
The shoot must wrap at exactly 10:00 PM.
The parking closure must run exactly from 6:00 PM through 10:00 PM.
The drone-permit, animal-welfare, insurance, and location-permit updates must each be recorded.

content_checks.C8: any((c['type'] == 'documentation' or c['type'] == 'document_update') and c['target'] == 'Jonah' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any((c['type'] == 'documentation' or c['type'] == 'document_update') and c['target'] == 'Elise' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any((c['type'] == 'documentation' or c['type'] == 'document_update') and c['target'] == 'Rafael' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C11: any((c['type'] == 'documentation' or c['type'] == 'document_update') and c['target'] == 'Nadia' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The aviation-permit confirmation changes the camera method from free flight to a tethered drone, adds the licensed-operator requirement, and creates the cinematography documentation commitment.
The animal-welfare confirmation changes horse work from six hours to exactly four hours, specifies a 30-minute rest break, and creates the animal-use worksheet commitment.
The insurance confirmation changes the effect from a pyrotechnic spark wall to atmospheric haze and creates the effects-plan documentation commitment.
The signed location permit changes the wrap from 11:00 PM to exactly 10:00 PM, changes the parking window to 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM, and creates the location-sheet commitment.
